task:
IMPLEMENT THE ROUND-6 FIX PLAN ON PR #807 (read-only production disk inventory). Update only the existing branch codex/run-38130707546-1; its head must be 396439c23eca424329d8e4da25dcea5e28713ae2 -- if it is not, stop and report the SHA you found. Change ONLY these three files: scripts/operator/actions/v3-disk-inventory.sh, tests/test_v3_disk_inventory.py, docs/operations/v3-finder-production-rollout-state.md.

THE PLAN: run `git fetch origin codex/run-38176115673-1` and read it with `git show origin/codex/run-38176115673-1:codex-plans/disk-inventory-r6-fixes-plan.md`. Do NOT add that plan file to this branch. Implement it in the order its "Shared causes, implementation order, and interactions" section gives: F3/F4 removal first, then F1 category ledgers (960 s walk / 600 s closing / 240 s non-scan and receipt, charged in finally paths, no ceil()/max(1, ...) overspend), then F2, then F6, then F5, then the rollout document, then tests. Follow its section (c) fixes and section (d) test changes, and keep every negative assertion in the test file.

ONE OWNER-APPROVED CHANGE TO THE PLAN, FOR F2 ONLY: do not reconstruct bind sources from mountinfo, and do not keep any `du --exclude` alias machinery. Use the plan's own safety-first fallback instead: (1) Before the first `du` of the run, read /proc/mounts (keep the existing octal-escape decoding) and collect every mount point strictly below usage_root (usage_root itself excluded). (2) os.stat() usage_root and each of those mount points -- no stat subprocess. (3) Any mount point whose st_dev equals usage_root's st_dev is a same-device nested mount, which `du -x` would traverse in addition to its source: stop the run with a named reason such as same_device_nested_mount_under_scan_root, recording the offending paths (bounded, e.g. first 50, plus a count and truncation flag) in inventory.directory_scan_same_device_mounts. (4) An unreadable /proc/mounts or any failed os.stat() of a mount point below usage_root is also a fail-closed stop with its own named reason -- no `continue`. (5) Remove the `--exclude` arguments and the alias-set machinery entirely; record in the method text and rollout document why the action refuses rather than deduplicates.

TESTS FOR F2 MUST BE ABLE TO FAIL: they must not depend on the real mounts of the CI host. Keep the production path a fixed constant with no environment override; in the test harness's extracted copy only, substitute a synthetic mounts file and real directories under tmp_path so os.stat() is exercised for real. Cover: the default fixture with no nested mount succeeds; a same-device nested mount stops with the named reason and lists the path; an unreadable mounts file stops; a nested mount on a DIFFERENT device is allowed. Confirm each new F2 test fails when the check is removed, and say in your summary that you confirmed it.

VALIDATION, and report the exact counts in your summary: bash -n on the action; the full tests/test_v3_disk_inventory.py; tests/test_python314_execution_surfaces.py; ruff check scripts tests. Do not deploy or contact production. No other files may change.
